lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Unit performance task: verifying tenancy rules locally

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic verifying tenancy rules locally task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: This performance task pulls together the whole unit.
safetyNotes: The housing options and sample lease used for the analysis portion are fictional; the learner does not need to disclose any real housing situation.
Research on tenancy rules should stay general (how rules can vary and how to verify them) and should not require entering personal information into any website to complete.
A guardian reviews the finished analysis and research before this lesson is marked complete.

simulationAlternative.description: If reliable local research sources aren't accessible when this lesson is done, the learner instead works from a provided general list of ways tenancy rules commonly vary (notice periods, deposit limits and return timelines, habitability requirements, and rent-increase rules) and explains, using only that provided list, how someone would go about verifying which specific rules apply to a place they're considering, discussing that reasoning with a guardian instead of completing live research.

materials: learner-local: the provided general list of ways tenancy rules commonly vary

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Now that you've completed the full analysis, what part of moving into a place of your own do you feel most prepared for, and what part would you still want a trusted adult's help with?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Analysis completeness and accuracy: All four components are present and accurately reflect the provided options and lease. | Research quality on tenancy-rule variation: Answer clearly explains two specific ways rules can vary and names one specific, workable verification method. | Guardian-reviewed self-assessment: Reflection names one specific part felt ready for and one specific part still needing help. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner research one additional way tenancy rules can differ (beyond the two already covered) and add it, with its own verification method, to their task 3 answer.

resources.title: verifying tenancy rules locally worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: This performance task pulls together the whole unit.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact verifying tenancy rules locally decision or action.
Model move 2: Before researching, name a current assumption you're not fully sure is accurate.

Model move 3: Complete the full housing analysis using the provided options and sample lease: a comparison of the three housing options, a summary of the sample lease's key obligations, a move-in checklist, and a one-month move-in budget that includes rent, the deposit, and at least two setup costs.

Model check: Analysis completeness and accuracy: All four components are present and accurately reflect the provided options and lease. | Research quality on tenancy-rule variation: Answer clearly explains two specific ways rules can vary and names one specific, workable verification method. | Guardian-reviewed self-assessment: Reflection names one specific part felt ready for and one specific part still needing help.

resources.title: verifying tenancy rules locally action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for verifying tenancy rules locally.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: verifying tenancy rules locally coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: This performance task pulls together the whole unit.
Coach direction: Before researching, name a current assumption you're not fully sure is accurate.
Learner prompt: Before researching, what do you currently assume is true about tenant rights or landlord rules that you're not fully sure is accurate?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: verifying tenancy rules locally complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Complete the full housing analysis using the provided options and sample lease: a comparison of the three housing options, a summary of the sample lease's key obligations, a move-in checklist, and a one-month move-in budget that includes rent, the deposit, and at least two setup costs.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Summarize your comparison of the three housing options and which one you'd recommend and why.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Summarize the sample lease's key obligations for the tenant and for the landlord.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I built a move-in checklist with at least six specific items.
Response 4 (t2-p4): List your one-month move-in budget, including rent, the deposit, and at least two setup costs, with a total.

Equal-access rule: If reliable local research sources aren't accessible when this lesson is done, the learner instead works from a provided general list of ways tenancy rules commonly vary (notice periods, deposit limits and return timelines, habitability requirements, and rent-increase rules) and explains, using only that provided list, how someone would go about verifying which specific rules apply to a place they're considering, discussing that reasoning with a guardian instead of completing live research.

resources.title: verifying tenancy rules locally minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Now that you've completed the full analysis, what part of moving into a place of your own do you feel most prepared for, and what part would you still want a trusted adult's help with?

Success checks: Analysis completeness and accuracy: All four components are present and accurately reflect the provided options and lease. | Research quality on tenancy-rule variation: Answer clearly explains two specific ways rules can vary and names one specific, workable verification method. | Guardian-reviewed self-assessment: Reflection names one specific part felt ready for and one specific part still needing help.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: verifying tenancy rules locally supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional verifying tenancy rules locally condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Analysis completeness and accuracy: All four components are present and accurately reflect the provided options and lease. | Research quality on tenancy-rule variation: Answer clearly explains two specific ways rules can vary and names one specific, workable verification method. | Guardian-reviewed self-assessment: Reflection names one specific part felt ready for and one specific part still needing help..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
